# spw.quest

> Spw is a notation for a reading you can compare: a mark says what a word is doing, and a brace says which slot it fills. An answer written in Spw can be parsed, compared, and opened as a card or a canvas.

An address and a line together, as in "spw.quest rpgwednesday<card>", ask for an answer written in Spw. The line names the subject and its <concept> names the kind of answer. An answer is plain Spw text, with no code fence and no sentence before it. A person setting up a repository wants [the recipe](https://spw.quest/init) instead.

A line is word[mode]{body}(scene)<concept>, and only the word is required.

- word: what the line is about, one name with no spaces.
- [mode]: how it is being seen.
- {body}: what belongs to it. A dot makes one name, a comma holds a company, a semicolon keeps an order, ~> is a path.
- (scene): where or when it stands.
- <concept>: what kind of thing it is.

A mark goes right before a word, with no space after it:

- ~ potential: Keep a path open without taking it.
- ? wonder: Open a question you can close again.
- ! action: Commit a move so its consequence can be seen.
- * value: Mark what carries weight here.
- . ground: Come back to the local default.
- ^ ascension: Lift parts into one relation you can inspect.
- # vibration: Name a structure so it can be found again.
- @ perspective: Say who is looking, and from where.
- & subject: Name what the relation is about.
- = configuration: Keep this here, under this name.
- % measure: Compare, weigh, or level the field.
- $ substrate: Name what carries the charge: time, money, memory, attention.

Quoted text takes double quotes. #>name names a file or a line, and #:kind says what kind of file it is.

A word<card> is the line with its [mode], {body} and (scene) filled in from what is known, then a seed card, and a seed card always names its template. For a thing you know about, ^seed[Session] has the fields date, scene, turn, carry and revisit, and a field with nothing known is left out. Asked garden<card>, this is an answer, and pasted on spwashi.com it opens as a card:

    garden[weekly]{beds, compost, seedlings}(saturday)<card>
    ^seed[Session]{
      scene: "a shared plot, tended on Saturdays"
      carry: "the beds planted last week"
      revisit: "what survived the frost?"
    }

For a word you know nothing about, not knowing is the card. ^seed[Wonder.Prompt] has the fields question, tension, material, relay and revisit, and each says what would have to be found out:

    nightmarket<card>
    ^seed[Wonder.Prompt]{
      question: "what is nightmarket, and who keeps it?"
      tension: "the name is all that was given"
      relay: "whoever named it"
      revisit: "once a page says what it is"
    }

A word<question> is the question, what is expected, and the probe that would answer it:

    ?["Will the seedlings survive a frost?"]{
      ~#expect: "the covered bed holds and the open bed does not"
      !probe{ "read both beds the morning after the first frost" }
    }

A word<change> says what happened, what changed, and how it was checked:

    #[episode]{
      ~[scene]{ the open bed lost its seedlings to a frost }
      ![change]{ every bed is covered before dusk in November }
      *[verify]{ all four beds came through the next frost }
    }

Any other <concept> is the line with its slots filled and one plain sentence:

    garden[weekly]{beds, compost}(saturday)<plot>
    *says = "a shared plot, tended on Saturdays"

Facts about a word come from the Card address below, which lists what the site holds for it. On X an answer fits 280 characters and has no @ directly before a name, since that notifies the account; a # before a letter shows as a tag. A link to https://spw.quest/card?line= with the line percent-encoded unfurls as a link card.

## Addresses

Every address below answers with a page that reads with no script, except Canvas.

- [Card](https://spw.quest/card.txt?line=rpgwednesday%3Ccard%3E): You hold a line and want what the site holds for its word before answering it, as text. line: one line, 200 characters. /card with the same line is a small page that unfurls as a link card, and spw.quest/ followed by the line itself answers the same. Example: line = rpgwednesday<card>.
- [Pivot](https://spw.quest/pivot?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You hold one line and want the lines one change away from it, grouped by the slot each turns. A turn that lands on a line a page already holds says which page, with a link to it. line: one line, 200 characters; past that it is cut and the page says so. In a browser, #turn-mode, #turn-body, #turn-subject, #turn-scope or #turn-projection scrolls to one slot; a fetch gets the whole page. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.
- [Find](https://spw.quest/specimens?q=recipe%5B*%5D): You want every line on spwashi.com with some shape: the same word through other lenses, the same lens on other words. q: slots to match, with * for any value. The page is about 280 KB whatever is asked: the answer comes first, and the whole shelf follows it. Example: q = recipe[*].
- [Compare](https://spw.quest/specimens?a=h-capsule&b=h-induct_join): You hold two shelf lines and want the slots they share and the slot where they part. a, b: shelf ids, as Find prints them. The page is about 280 KB whatever is asked: the answer comes first, and the whole shelf follows it. Example: a = h-capsule, b = h-induct_join.
- [Take apart](https://spw.quest/build?script=~door%5Bajar%5D%7Bhinge%7D): You hold a file, or a line among others, and want what a tool reads from it and each slot's alternatives from the file's own lines. script: up to 1800 characters in an address. line: which of its lines to take apart, counted from 1. Example: script = ~door[ajar]{hinge}.
- [Read a file](https://spw.quest/?example=record): You want a whole example of a kind of file (a log, a catalog record, a question with its probe) and what a tool reads from it. example: notebook, record, vocabulary, question, script, revision, persona, calibration, perspectives, loops, gradient, syntax, headings, perform, outline, recurrence, laws, pantry, pipeline, review, records, surfaces, primitives, algorithms, role or onboarding. at: a name in the file, to land on its line. Example: example = record.
- [Check a line](https://spw.quest/read?step=act&line=~door): You are learning one mark and want a single line checked against that panel's rule. step: write, act, hold, name, point, ask or grow. line: up to 400 characters. Example: step = act, line = ~door.
- [At rest](https://spw.quest/physics?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You want a line drawn as bodies at rest, with the laws that placed them. line: one line. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.
- [Canvas](https://spw.quest/canvas?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You want a person to see a line laid out as a force-directed canvas on factshift.center. It draws with scripts, so a reader without them gets only its chrome: use Pivot to read the line. line: up to 400 characters, or s: a shelf id. Answers with a redirect to factshift.center. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.

## Reference

- [Marks and braces](https://spw.quest/#operators): each mark and brace pair, what it reads as, and what the runtime does with it.
- [Constructs](https://spw.quest/constructs): the shapes a line takes, each with a pressed example.
- [Dated parser builds](https://spw.quest/parser/): the parser as a file to load on your own page.

## Optional

- [Initialize a repository](https://spw.quest/init): the recipe for mounting Spw Workbench, for an agent asked to set one up.
- [quest.json](https://spw.quest/quest.json): that recipe's facts as data.
- [Every example file](https://spw.quest/llms-full.txt): this index, then each file whole.
